No fabricated or unsupported quotes were found. Three quotes (LTM '(LTM)' vs source's '(“LTM”)', the Seller-Note '(the Seller Note)' vs source's '(the “Seller Note”)', and the NASA '(IXPE)' vs source's '(“IXPE”)') drop SEC-style scare-quotes around a defined term — cosmetic, not substantive. One quote ('...to repay the Seller Note in full...') splices across a page-break running header ('Page 84 Table of Contents REDWIRE CORPORATION NOTES...') that Workiva's paginated HTML inserts mid-sentence — the underlying sentence is continuous in the actual financial-statement text; this is a rendering artifact, not a misquote.

refuted_claims.claim: FY2025 book-to-bill ratio of 1.32x (Space 1.13x / Defense Tech 1.62x) reflects organic demand growth vs. 0.76x in FY2024.
refuted_claims.evidence: The 10-K's own MD&A discloses that the LTM-ended-12/31/2025 'contracts awarded' numerator used to compute 1.32x includes $73.7 million of acquired (not newly-won) contract value carried over from the Edge Autonomy acquisition (closed 6/13/2025). Recomputing without it: ($441.478M total contracts awarded - $73.7M) / $335.381M total revenue ≈ 1.10x organic, materially below the 1.32x headline. The FY2024 comparison base (0.76x) is itself not clean either — it includes $21.9M of acquired contract value from the Hera Systems acquisition. This inorganic layer is not flagged anywhere in the DD's binding_demand narrative. Partially offsetting: the 10-Q separately discloses that the more current LTM-ended-6/30/2026 book-to-bill of 1.52x is explicitly stated to be organic ('none of the contracts awarded balance relates to acquired contract value'), so the H1-2026 growth trend the DD leans on is not undermined — only the single FY2025 headline ratio is.
refuted_claims.citation: 10-K, 2026-02-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000029/rdw-20251231.htm: 'For the LTM ended December 31, 2025, contracts awarded includes $73.7 million of acquired contract value from the Edge Autonomy acquisition... For the LTM ended December 31, 2024, contracts awarded includes $21.9 million of acquired contract value from the Hera Systems acquisition.' Corroborating (organic figure): 10-Q, 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000124/rdw-20260630.htm: 'For the LTM ended June 30, 2026 none of the contracts awarded balance relates to acquired contract value.'

refuted_claims.claim: binding_demand verdict of 'confirmed_delivered' treats historical/heritage fielding (Stalker 'proven... for two decades', NASA missions already flown) as equivalent evidentiary weight to current, revenue-generating demand.
refuted_claims.evidence: Most of the named-customer evidence (Marine Corps/Army/Five Eyes, Ukraine/Latvia heritage, NASA DART/Artemis/IXPE) is legacy/heritage marketing language about hardware fielded or missions flown in the past, not current signed contracts or forward backlog for those specific customers. The only current-period, dollar-quantified demand evidence in the filing is the backlog/book-to-bill figures (addressed above) and the Customer D/E revenue-concentration table — and the DD's own entry for Customer D/E correctly labels bindingness 'unknown.' Collapsing heritage narrative and current binding demand into a single 'confirmed_delivered' verdict overstates how much of the underlying evidence is forward-looking vs. retrospective.
refuted_claims.citation: 10-K, 2026-02-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000029/rdw-20251231.htm: 'meeting mission needs for customers including, but not limited to, the U.S. Marine Corps, U.S. Army, and Five Eyes partners' (heritage framing); 'successfully deployed on several flight missions in LEO, GEO, and deep space, including on the ISS, NASA's Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (“IXPE”) mission, and NASA's DART mission' (past-tense, completed missions).

missed_disqualifiers.gate: Item 5.02 / governance-remediation obligation tied to the material-weakness litigation
missed_disqualifiers.evidence: The investigator's own graveyard_gates.short_seller_or_litigation entry cites only the $0.9M fee order from the 10-Q's litigation note. A dedicated 8-K (Item 8.01), not in the investigator's filings_read list, discloses that the Yingling v. Cannito derivative-suit settlement is not purely monetary: it requires Redwire to 'adopt certain corporate governance reforms' as a condition of dismissal — i.e., a court-supervised governance remediation obligation flowing directly from the pre-2023 internal-control allegations, layered on top of the currently-disclosed, unremediated Edge Autonomy/European material weakness. This strengthens rather than weakens the material-weakness gate the DD already flagged; it was simply never cited.
missed_disqualifiers.citation: 8-K, 2026-06-18, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000081/rdw-20260618.htm: 'the proposed settlement calls for the Company to adopt certain corporate governance reforms, as described further in the Stipulation, and pay attorneys’ fees and expenses, which the Company expects to be funded by its insurance carrier, in exchange for a full and complete release and dismissal of the derivative actions.'

missed_disqualifiers.gate: warrant (pre-existing dilutive instrument not disclosed in last_raise.discount_and_warrants)
missed_disqualifiers.evidence: The DD states 'No warrants issued in the ATM or June 2025 offering' — true and unrefuted for those two transactions specifically — but does not disclose that Redwire has separate, pre-existing 2021 de-SPAC-era public and private warrants outstanding (AEI alone held 2,000,000 private warrants as of both 12/31/2025 and 2/23/2026, exercisable at $11.50/share) that were still live as of the FY2025 10-K and expired only weeks before this review's as-of date. This is a minor, now largely-resolved dilution vector the DD's 'no warrants' framing could be read as ruling out entirely.
missed_disqualifiers.citation: 10-K, 2026-02-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000029/rdw-20251231.htm: 'In September 2021, the Company issued 7,732,168 private warrants... entitle the holder to purchase one share of common stock at an exercise price of $11.50 per share... The warrants will expire on September 2, 2026'; 'AEI owned 85,473,375 shares of our outstanding common stock and 2,000,000 of our private warrants and as of February 23, 2026, these amounts have reduced to 45,073,029 and 2,000,000, respectively.'

missed_disqualifiers.gate: going concern (unconfirmed — flagged for transparency, not asserted as a finding)
missed_disqualifiers.evidence: EDGAR full-text search for the exact phrase 'going concern' restricted to CIK 1819810 / forms 10-K,10-Q,8-K / 2025-09-26 to 2026-09-26 returns 2 hits beyond the 10-K/10-Q that graveyard_gates already checked: the credit-agreement exhibits to the 8-Ks dated 2026-02-25 and 2026-07-01 (Amended and Restated Credit Agreement and its Amendment No. 1). These multi-hundred-page loan-agreement exhibits were not fetched or read in this review — the phrase most plausibly sits inside standard 'financial statements prepared on a going-concern basis' representations/covenants that are boilerplate in every syndicated credit agreement, not a company-specific doubt. This is reported as an open item, not a confirmed disqualifier: it should not be treated as evidence of going-concern doubt without reading the actual clause.
missed_disqualifiers.citation: EDGAR full-text search, https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22going%20concern%22&ciks=0001819810&forms=10-K,10-Q,8-K&dateRange=custom&startdt=2025-09-26&enddt=2026-09-26 — hits: 0001819810-26-000017:exhibit101amendedandrestat.htm (8-K filed 2026-02-25) and 0001819810-26-000084:exhibit101amendmentno1toam.htm (8-K filed 2026-07-01).

other_findings_not_disqualifying.note: Two credit-agreement 8-Ks (2026-02-25: JPM Amended & Restated Credit Agreement, refinanced/repaid the older Adams Street Credit Agreement in full, term loan maturity extended 2027->2029, SOFR+3.25-3.75% margin; 2026-07-01: Amendment No.1, revolver increased $30M->$50M and a $40M voluntary prepayment cut the term loan from $90M to $50M) were not in the investigator's filings_read list. Both are favorable — real deleveraging using ATM proceeds, not covenant distress — and corroborate rather than contradict the DD's capital_web_edges entry for the JPMorgan lender relationship. Cited for completeness, not as a disqualifier.

Cash and cash equivalents rose from $76.5M (12/31/2025) to $557.0M (6/30/2026), entirely a balance-sheet-date figure driven by the ATM draws already disclosed in last_raise — no evidence was found that any 'runway' figure in the DD relies on post-6/30/2026 ATM proceeds. The 10-Q's liquidity statement is the standard 'sufficient... for at least the next twelve months' formula with no going-concern qualifier, consistent with graveyard_gates.going_concern_explicit = No.
other_findings_not_disqualifying.citation: 10-Q, 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000124/rdw-20260630.htm: 'We believe our existing sources of liquidity will be sufficient to meet our working capital needs and debt service obligations and to comply with our debt covenants for at least the next twelve months from the date on which our condensed consolidated financial statements were issued.'

other_findings_not_disqualifying.note: Full-text searches for 'substantial doubt', 'minimum bid price', 'Listing Rule', and 'registered direct' over CIK 1819810 / 10-K,10-Q,8-K / trailing 12 months each returned 0 hits, independently corroborating graveyard_gates.going_concern_explicit and .listing_notice_12m and last_raise's characterization of the ATM/follow-on as open-market, non-PIPE issuance.

band_reason: The two gates the investigator leaned on are real, correctly cited, and if anything slightly understated rather than overstated: the material weakness is unremediated across three consecutive filings (10-K 12/31/25, plus confirmed still-open per the 10-Q 6/30/26) and is now tied by a freshly-found 8-K to a court-mandated corporate-governance-reform settlement stemming from a pre-2023 controls failure — not a one-off integration hiccup but a recurring pattern; and the related-party PE sponsor's exit was both faster and larger than the single 13D/A trajectory the DD cited (AEI alone held 85.5M shares + 2M warrants as of 12/31/2025, already down to 45.1M shares by 2/23/2026, before AE Red Holdings' tracked drop from 19.7% to 1.1% between 1/9/26 and 5/18/26) — a founder/seller who was just paid ~49.8M shares for Edge Autonomy fully exiting within months, while the company simultaneously ran three back-to-back ATM facilities (+73.6% share count YoY). Against that: fundamentals are genuinely improving on both an as-reported and an organic basis (the one favorable number that was inflated — FY2025 book-to-bill 1.32x vs. an organic ~1.10x — is a modest overstatement, not a fabrication, and the more recent LTM book-to-bill of 1.52x is confirmed organic by the company itself), debt was refinanced and then paid down $40M using equity proceeds, and none of the harder disqualifiers (going-concern doubt, delisting notice, SEC investigation, restatement, PIPE/registered-direct/warrant-laden dilutive financing) are present. On balance the two structural gates the pattern is designed to catch — an unremediated controls gate plus a complete, rapid insider/related-party exit coinciding with the growth story that exit was riding on — are both real and well-evidenced, which is enough to keep this in avoid-pattern rather than downgrade to watch-thin or abstain, but the unusually strong, largely-organic underlying fundamentals are the reason this is a closer call than the DD's flat framing suggests.
